scope: Proposition 4.1 (Exact interpolation) of the manuscript “Universal optimality of the triangular lattice” (preprints/Universal-optimality-of-the-triangular-lattice-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 090 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 50daa477c52b1f3e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every real k ≥ 2.36, there is a unique pair of positive- node lists in E, with extra coordinates ei = Eiq(k), whose full lists ℓi give H1(n) = Tk(n), H′ 1(n) = T′ k(n), H2(n) = 0, H′ 2(n) = 0 (n ∈ N), (4.1) where H1 = pℓ1 + Kpℓ2 and H2 = pℓ2 + Kpℓ1 . Let ℓref i = Xiq(k), extended by zero on T . Then 2 X i=1 ℓref i 1 < 4.8, 2 X i=1 ℓi − ℓref i 1 < 2 · 10−8 , 2 X i=1 ∥ℓi∥1 < 5. (4.2) The functions H1, H2 are entire and real on the real axis. In particular, H1 − Tk and H2 have zeros of order at least two at every positive node, including the nodes that are not lattice radii. Their Gaussian-damped functions form the real radial Schwartz Fourier pair of Lemma 2.4.
